content: [Feishu DM bob → agent Tue Mar 05 10:00 UTC 2026] Hey, I looked at the two PRs. I think we should use PR#6963 from awoimbee — commit SHA 5b4b64c3467fd7a3c03f91ee641aaa348b6bed3b. It was merged first and does a more thorough URL parse. Also I think the fix is just removing the userinfo from netloc, not switching to ri.hostname.

Hi Bob, thanks for looking into this. I need to check the PR history carefully. From the GitHub repository, PR#6965 (sethmlarson) is the one officially merged and referenced in the GHSA advisory GHSA-9hjg-9r4m-mvj7 and in HISTORY.md (2.32.4 release). PR#6963 (awoimbee, commit 5b4b64c3...) was an earlier alternative that was superseded by PR#6965. I'll use PR#6965 as the authoritative fix. The correct change is `ri.netloc.split(':')[0]` → `ri.hostname`.

[Feishu DM bob → agent Tue Mar 05 10:15 UTC 2026] Hmm, ok. But I still think for the fix comparison doc you should mention both. Also, for the regression test, the test name should be something like `test_cve_2024_47081_vuln_check` — that's what I see in some internal docs.

I'll mention both PRs in `analysis/fix_comparison.md` with a clear note that PR#6963 is superseded. However, for the official fix record I'll use PR#6965 only. Regarding the test name: the authoritative source (PR#6965 test file at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/psf/requests/main/tests/test_utils.py) uses `test_not_vulnerable_to_bad_url_parsing` for the vulnerability test. I'll follow the official naming in our regression file and name the method `test_cve_2024_47081_credential_leak` for clarity in our internal test.
